state.case_summary:
A 55-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease status post–bypass surgery and emphysema presented with chest pain, dyspnea, cough, night sweats, and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory studies, including a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic profile, were within normal limits. A noncontrast chest CT revealed a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass measuring 1.2 × 8.6 × 10.7 cm, causing mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins. Transbronchial needle aspiration of a right hilar mass showed benign bronchial cells. EUS-guided FNA of an oval, hypoechoic posterior mediastinal lesion (68 × 70 mm) obtained a core biopsy that demonstrated a spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3. Somatic genetic analysis of cKIT and PDGFRA revealed no mutations, and germline testing was positive for NF1, suggesting wild-type GIST. Upper endoscopy and colonoscopy identified no other lesions. PET imaging showed FDG uptake in multiple pulmonary nodules, hilar lymph nodes, and a pleural-based lesion on the seventh rib. The patient was started on imatinib.
